post_text:
I am a JVM veteran who feared the cold start.

I optimized our serverless functions to be lightning-fast. ⚡

I assumed static initializers were the perfect place for business configuration.

The P99 latency dropped significantly, and the dashboards stayed green.

The system looked flawless, and I felt like a hero.

But I noticed a tiny, recurring jitter in the startup logs that I ignored.

Weeks later, a finance audit flagged a massive data discrepancy.

Because the JVMs stayed warm for days, they never refreshed their static state.

We processed thousands of transactions using stale pricing logic.

The system was incredibly fast, but it was consistently wrong. 📉

My optimization created a silent drift in business reality.

The customer support team spent weeks manually correcting invoices for angry users. 🛠️

The damage was invisible because the health checks only measured speed.

We won the latency war but lost the integrity battle.

The Moral 👇

A fast response time is a liability when the underlying state has silently expired.
